Newspoll AC Nielsen Morgan Galaxy Trove

Trove newspaper poll archive

Every newspaper article in the National Library's Trove archive that mentions a poll — 3,047,897 articles, 1803-01 to 2025-12, harvested through Trove's own search API — and the 7,868 poll reports extracted from them.

This page exists for safekeeping and for verification. The polling series the tracker compares against — Morgan, Nielsen, Newspoll and the rest — were read in print before they were ever published online; for the years the pollsters' own sites don't reach back to, the newspaper of record is the only published source left. Trove's digitisation window is the coverage: state mastheads to the mid-1950s, The Canberra Times to 1995, and little after that but government gazettes.

Coverage over time

Articles matching "( poll )" per decade. "About polling" is the subset written in poll-figures language (opinion poll, two-party-preferred, primary vote …); "poll reports" name a pollster. The 1990s row stops at 1995 — that is when the newspapers leave copyright clearance, not when polling stopped.

The poll reports

7,868 articles that name a pollster. Every row links to the article on Trove, where the scan and corrected text are public. The full set is in trove-poll-articles.csv; the monthly tallies behind the first table are in trove-mentions-monthly.csv. Full OCR text for 3167 articles of them is mirrored in trove-text.jsonl.

How this was collected

Everything on this page is reproducible from the crawler in the repo. The parts, because Trove's own documentation does not describe the route this site uses:

  1. The API. The trove.nla.gov.au web app talks to its own JSON API: GET /api/search/137?terms=( poll )&limits={"date.from":[from],"date.to":[to]}&pageSize=100&startPos=n. Records come back in works[]. Each record carries the article's id, title, masthead, date, page, word count, abstract and search snippets.
  2. The header. The search authorises with an apikey header carrying the site's own public client key — the key shipped to every visitor's browser, captured by watching the page's own requests (page.on('request') in headless Chrome), not a secret and not the registered-developer API. If it ever rotates, re-capture it from the site the same way, or set TROVE_API_KEY.
  3. The 5000-record wall. No query returns past startPos 5000, and a heavy month (March 1901) holds more than that — so the crawler splits any over-cap window in half, down to single days. Nothing is deduplicated across windows; ids are unique per window, and windows never overlap.
  4. The full text. Every record has a corrected-OCR text rendition at /newspaper/rendition/nla.news-article<ID>.txt. .build/harvest-trove-text.mjs fetches these for the poll reports; the text is committed (trove-text.jsonl) only while the bundle fits the repo's data-file norm — 3167 articles, 8.4 MB at last refresh.

Re-run the whole harvest (resumable; months land in .matilda/trove-harvest/):

node .build/harvest-trove.mjs 1803 2025
node .build/harvest-trove-text.mjs     # OCR text for the poll reports
node .build/refresh-trove-archive.mjs  # this page + the two CSVs

Known limits

The corpus is everything Trove's search matches for the token poll in the newspaper category — that includes polling booths and opinion polls alike, which is the triage the two smaller subsets do. OCR is machine-read and corrected by volunteers; titles from the 1800s especially keep stray misreadings. The gazette tail after 1995 is government printing, not news. And the corpus is a snapshot: the National Library keeps scanning, so a re-run will find more, never less.

This is a satellite archive page of auspol tracker, an unofficial aggregate of published federal opinion polling. The live, interactive tracker carries the current aggregates, charts and per-poll archive.
